title: Week of July 6–12
subtitle: Week 4 · Deload — key lifts back off ~10-15%, mileage down ~30%, clear Weeks 2-3 fatigue before the next build block.
goals: Deload: squat/bench/deadlift/OHP ease back ~10-15% off last week's tops — clean reps, no grinding.
Mileage down to ~10 mi this week (from ~14); Tuesday's quality run is shorter too — still the one hard session.
More core variety this week (Bird Dog, Pallof Press, Woodchopper, Suitcase Carry) — per your note.
Protein ≥180g daily; stay inside the 2200 kcal target — trending well (199.4→195.3 lb since 6/18).
review: Week 3 was a strong build: squat hit 200 (Good, though form loosened on the last rep), RDL exceeded to 205 but your back felt tight — noted. Bench nailed 190 (Good, 1-2 RIR held) and OHP got pushed to 125, but that turned into a push press — too heavy, pulling it back. Barbell row (145) and lat pulldown (150) both moved up and felt good. Deadlift hit a shockingly good 275, and switching goblet→front squat clearly worked (125, way more effort at the same reps) — keeping front squat going forward. Tuesday's hard run averaged HR 167 — that's expected and by design for your one hard session each week, not a red flag, but this week's version is trimmed to match the deload. Weekly mileage landed close to plan (~14 mi), acute:chronic ratio came out to ~1.37 (just over the 1.3 caution line), and this lands right on the Week-4 deload slot in the 3-4 week cadence — so mileage backs off ~30% and key lifts ease ~10-15% this week to bank recovery before the next build block. On your note that the run progression feels slow: understood — you handled ~30 mi/wk before, but that volume is exactly what preceded the crash driving this rebuild, so we're staying disciplined on the ramp for now; once this deload clears, the build rate picks back up. Added core variety per your ask (Bird Dog, Pallof Press, Woodchopper, Suitcase Carry mixed in, staples like Plank/Ab Wheel held). Weight trending well: 199.4→195.3 lb since 6/18, on pace for the mid-Aug goal. No HRV/sleep/resting-HR synced this week — worth checking your wearable sync if that continues.
